question: If apparent halo gravity is baryonic gravity redirected through the cluster, do discrete galaxies, continuous starlight, or hot-gas morphology supply the direction that best predicts raw RX J2129 multiple-image positions?

field_law.carrier: P0599 deflection minus baryons-only GR deflection
field_law.route_map: Move a normalized copy of each member launch weight by L=0.25 R80 along an observed component-attraction direction and smooth the landing map by w=0.50 R80
field_law.monopole_rule: Remove the convergence mean in every one-arcsecond annulus and independently subtract the circular radial-deflection mean
field_law.axisymmetric_gate: This angular layer is defined to be zero for a one-source Solar field and for the one-dimensional axisymmetric SPARC profiles
field_law.absolute_mass_limit: F160W and Chandra maps choose direction only; neither flux nor X-ray count rate is treated as an absolute mass

component_directions.definition: pairwise attraction toward discrete hard photometric members
attraction toward registered HST F160W positive light
attraction toward registered point-source-masked Chandra 0.7-2.0 keV morphology
unit-vector blend of 50% starlight and 50% gas direction
50% member direction plus 50% of an equal starlight/gas direction blend

selection.screen_source_positions: profiled on the 15 training images separately for every component/amplitude
selection.screen_metric: exact lens-equation root RMS at fixed geometry
selection.positive_candidate: lowest training RMS among s_theta>0 candidates with all 15 training roots
selection.signed_control: lowest training RMS among s_theta<0 candidates with all 15 training roots

cross_domain_controls.galaxy_reference: P0599; angular component layer is exactly absent on catalogued axisymmetric profiles
cross_domain_controls.Solar_reference: P0599 Solar proxies pass; a one-source angular route is identically absent

claim_limits: Every RX J2129 image is spent; training-only selection prevents direct leakage but does not make the held-out result fresh.
F160W traces light rather than stellar mass and Chandra brightness traces emissivity rather than gas mass.
The component maps set only route direction; the angular strength grid is a post-audit mechanism bracket, not a fitted universal constant.
The raw lens model still refits six ordinary pseudo-elliptical geometry and shear parameters.
A projected thin-lens correction cannot determine the hidden height or time history of a gravity arc.
A favorable RX J2129 component must transfer unchanged to a different raw cluster before it can be treated as evidence.
